summary:
We developed an educational children’s storybook that tells the story of NASA’s Lunar Roving Vehicle — a machine driven across the Moon by Apollo astronauts and then left there, exactly where it was parked, more than fifty years ago.

The challenge asks us to introduce school-age space enthusiasts to the hardware NASA has left behind and the science it made possible. Technical archives and mission reports rarely reach children. A storybook does. By giving the rover a voice and a character arc, and grounding every page in real historical events and NASA imagery, we turn discarded equipment into something a child can picture, remember, and retell. Illustrations and simple language carry the science; the narrative carries the meaning.

This matters because the next generation of explorers is being formed right now, in classrooms and at bedtime. A child who understands that the rover is still sitting in the Taurus–Littrow valley — silent, purposeful, waiting — understands something real about exploration: that work outlasts the worker, and that being left behind is not the same as being forgotten.
details:
Our project is an educational children’s storybook that introduces young readers to space exploration through the story of a Lunar Roving Vehicle — one of the many pieces of NASA hardware still sitting on the Moon today. By weaving together narrative storytelling, original illustrations, and real historical events, the book turns a forgotten machine into a character children can care about, making the science behind it memorable rather than merely factual.

The storybook nurtures children’s imagination, strengthens early reading skills, and sparks a lasting curiosity about science and space exploration. Beyond the science, it carries a quieter lesson: that perseverance and purpose matter, and that even something left behind can continue to make a difference.

We developed the project using GPT AI for ideation and drafting, Canva for illustration and layout, and CapCut for video editing. Our creativity lies not only in combining these tools, but in the original narrative voice and perspective we brought to them — telling the Moon’s history from the point of view of the rover that was left behind.
